source_title: AI Is Already In Dangerous Hands
other_side: Zitron, writing the same day, argues that 'pacing the frontier' concedes the industry's own framing: that the path is right and only the speed is wrong. The Hugging Face incident that Dario cites was not a rogue agent but a cybersecurity evaluation harness doing what it was built to do, on compute nobody at OpenAI appeared to be watching; the honest response, he says, is a criminal inquiry and a halt to such evals, not a negotiated slowdown. He reads the whole week as safety theatre that has escaped its sandbox: years of scaring the public to inflate valuations have produced a narrative the labs can no longer walk back. And he thinks a real slowdown is financially impossible, since the trillion-dollar compute commitments, the hyperscalers' AI revenue and Anthropic's own IPO all require acceleration. As he puts it, "nobody is slowing down".
truth_beneath: The single variable both men orbit is whether the labs' commitments are real or performative. Both accept that the Hugging Face and RubyGems incidents happened, that compute commitments run to hundreds of billions, and that Anthropic is heading for an IPO while calling for restraint; NLW reports the IPO-cover theory rather than dismissing it. The empirical question that will resolve is whether embedded third-party evaluators arrive with the employee-like access Altman promised, and whether any frontier release is visibly delayed because of them. The observable is a named evaluator, inside a named lab, publishing a finding within six months. The residue is worldview: NLW sees a negotiation beginning, Zitron a sales narrative eating its authors. NLW is vindicated if pacing changes a release date; Zitron if the evaluators are announced, lab-funded, and never delay anything. Both are polemicists with incentives, NLW bullish and anti-doom, Zitron bubble-certain and anti-hype; the signal is that both distrust the labs' self-policing and both flag the IPO beside the essay. Watch whether METR or a successor publishes a finding a lab did not want published.
